newsitem.title: UK: UK wool sale sees halfbred hogs spin higher.
newsitem.headline: UK wool sale sees halfbred hogs spin higher.

text.p: The second Scottish sale of 1997 saw moderate price increases led by halfbred hogs after solid competition cleared eighty-five percent of the 2.25 million kg catalogue, the British Wool Marketing Board reported.
Spokesperson Liz Ambler said the Board was still on target to sell all of the current (1996-7) clip in the same year with no carryover into next season despite losing ground earlier in January.
"Although we will have sold three-quarters of the current clip by the end of February, prices are not moving much," she said.
Wednesday's auction saw the biggest gains for Best Cheviots and Halfbred Hogs which increased their value by five percent since the last Scottish sale on January 8, the Board's brokers reported.
Other Cheviot and Halfbred types were fully firm and Crosses and Blackfaces both gained 2.5 percent. --London Newsroom, +44 171 542 8071
